Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Case 9
Age: 6 months 18 days
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment: None

Hospital Course:
Case 9, a 6-month-old boy, was admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and management of his medical conditions. He was diagnosed with epilepsy, infantile spasms, developmental delay, and obesity. During his hospital stay, he underwent genetic testing to identify the underlying cause of his conditions.

Diagnostic Results:
The test results showed a de novo heterozygous missense variant in GABRB3. This variant is associated with epileptic encephalopathy, early infantile, 43 (EIEE43), a rare autosomal dominant disease. The patient's variant was classified as pathogenic according to the ACMG guidelines. This mutation of the GABRB3 gene is predicted to impact receptor function.

Treatment and Plan:
No treatment was initiated during the patient's hospital stay. The medical team provided the family with a comprehensive report on the results of the diagnostic test and the possible long-term implications of the diagnosis. The patient will continue to receive close medical follow-up and monitoring.

Follow-up:
The patient's family was advised to schedule a follow-up appointment with their primary care physician or a specialist in pediatric neurology to discuss the patient's care plan and the need for any further evaluations or testing.

Overall Impression:
Case 9 is a 6-month-old boy diagnosed with epilepsy, infantile spasms, developmental delay, and obesity. The diagnostic test identified a rare de novo heterozygous missense variant in GABRB3, classified as pathogenic, which is linked to epileptic encephalopathy, early infantile 43 (EIEE43). No treatment was initiated during the hospital stay, and the patient's family has been advised to schedule a follow-up appointment with a specialist in pediatric neurology to discuss the implications of the diagnosis and the patient's care plan.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is GABRB3-related early infantile epileptic encephalopathy (EIEE43), which presents with infantile spasms. It belongs to Chapter G, diseases of the nervous system. It is coded under epilepsy, category G40, since infantile spasms (West syndrome) fall under G40.4.

CODE: G40
